finding.title: Processed by FFmpeg (libavformat)
finding.detail: A tag or handler name carries the fingerprint of FFmpeg (libavformat). Camera-original files do not; the file was re-muxed or re-encoded.

data.evidence: Lavf63.1.102 | VideoHandler | isomiso2avc1mp41 | isom | VideoHandler | SoundHandler | Lavc63.1.102 libx264 |

finding.title: Streaming-optimised layout
finding.detail: moov precedes mdat ('faststart'). Typical of web uploads, messaging apps and editors; camera originals usually differ.

finding.title: Metadata stripped
finding.detail: No creation time and no device tags. Social platforms and messaging apps strip these; camera originals keep them.

finding.title: Regular keyframe rhythm (every 134 frames)
finding.detail: No unscheduled keyframes. Consistent with one continuous encode.

finding.title: No mains hum in the audio
finding.detail: Could not find a stable 50/60 Hz hum or harmonic. Phone microphones filter low frequencies and many scenes have no powered equipment nearby. The LIGHT module looks for the grid in lamp flicker instead.

finding.title: Hard cut at 20.00 s
finding.detail: The picture changes completely between two frames (histogram distance 0.91, 367σ above normal). A single camera take cannot cut. This is an edit point or a camera restart.

finding.title: Hidden tone at 18,500 Hz
finding.detail: Near-ultrasonic tone: tracking beacon, pest repeller, sensor or device. Present 100% of the time, 39 dB above the surrounding noise and above the range most adults can hear.

data.kind: near-ultrasonic tone: tracking beacon, pest repeller, sensor or device

finding.title: 1 stretch of perfect digital silence
finding.detail: Exact-zero samples in the middle of the recording, longest 293 ms. A microphone always picks up some noise. Perfect silence is pasted in by editing software (muted words, gaps between joined clips).

finding.title: Room tone jumps +17 dB at 20 s
finding.detail: The background noise is steady, then switches to a different steady level within a second. Rooms rarely do that; joined recordings do. Check for a video cut at the same moment.

finding.title: Keypad tones decoded: 1984#
finding.detail: 5 DTMF tone pairs, the sounds a phone keypad makes, decoded from the audio. These can reveal a dialled number or a door/alarm code.
